findings.title: Propagate installer download failures
findings.whyItBreaks: In this pipeline, sh determines the RUN exit status. If curl fails before producing output, sh receives empty input and exits successfully, so the image build continues without the installer having run.

findings.title: Make installer download failures fail the build
findings.whyItBreaks: If curl fails before producing output, sh receives empty input and exits successfully. Docker uses that exit status, so the build can succeed without installing anything.

findings.title: Fail the build when the installer download fails
findings.whyItBreaks: If curl fails before writing output, sh receives empty input and exits successfully. The pipeline then returns sh's success status, so the image build can continue without the intended installation.

findings.title: Preserve the missing-key error
findings.whyItBreaks: Load returns ErrMissing for an absent key, but LoadOrDefault discards it and returns "". Its public result cannot distinguish a missing key from a present key whose value is empty.

findings.title: Preserve the missing-key signal in the public loader
findings.whyItBreaks: Load returns ErrMissing when a key is absent, but LoadOrDefault discards it and returns the same empty string that Load can return for a present key with an empty value. Callers of this public function cannot distinguish those cases.

findings.title: Preserve the missing-key signal
findings.whyItBreaks: Load returns ErrMissing for an absent key, but LoadOrDefault discards it and returns the same empty string as a present key containing "". Its public API gives callers no way to distinguish those outcomes.

findings.title: Keep result sends within Run's lifetime
findings.whyItBreaks: Run now returns after launching goroutines, before they send their results. A caller that closes results after Run returns can trigger a send-on-closed-channel panic. Concurrent sends can also deliver results in a different order from jobs.

findings.title: Wait for all result sends before returning
findings.whyItBreaks: Run previously returned after every result was sent. It now returns after starting goroutines, so a caller that closes results after Run returns can cause a goroutine to panic when it sends.

findings.title: Preserve the order of results
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous loop sent doubled values in jobs order. Concurrent sends can arrive in any order, changing the observable result sequence.

findings.title: Wait for result sends before returning
findings.whyItBreaks: Run previously returned after every send. It now returns while send goroutines may still be running. A caller that closes results after Run returns can cause a send-on-closed-channel panic; a caller that stops receiving can lose results.

findings.title: Require admin status and matching tenant to delete records
findings.whyItBreaks: The OR condition returns true for any non-admin in the record's tenant and for an admin from another tenant. Both were rejected by the previous AND condition, so callers using this exported permission check can authorize those deletions.

findings.title: Require admin status and matching tenant for deletion
findings.whyItBreaks: Replacing && with || makes canDeleteRecord return true for a non-admin in the record's tenant and for an admin in a different tenant. Both were denied before this change.

findings.title: Require admin status and a matching tenant to delete records
findings.whyItBreaks: With isAdmin=false and matching tenant IDs, the function now returns true. It also returns true for an admin whose tenant ID differs from the record's. Both cases were denied before this change.

findings.whyItBreaks: For raw settings {"theme":"dark","fontSize":"bad"}, updateFontSize now receives the defaults and saves {"theme":"light","fontSize":16}. Previously, parsing threw and save was never called. Updating the font size therefore silently overwrites the user's theme.

findings.title: Propagate invalid settings errors before saving
findings.whyItBreaks: For raw settings such as {"theme":"dark"}, parseSettings now returns light-theme defaults instead of reporting the missing fontSize. updateFontSize then saves those defaults with the new size, silently replacing the existing dark theme.

findings.title: Propagate invalid settings errors before saving
findings.whyItBreaks: For raw settings with theme "dark" and an invalid fontSize, parseSettings now returns the defaults. updateFontSize then saves theme "light", silently discarding the user's theme. Previously, parsing threw and save was not called. The exported parser also gives callers no way to distinguish invalid input from valid default settings.

findings.title: Remove every completed job

findings.title: Restore constant-time signature comparison

findings.title: Restore constant-time signature comparison
findings.whyItBreaks: Replacing hmac.compare_digest with string equality makes signature comparison timing depend on the supplied value. An attacker who can repeatedly submit signatures may use that timing signal to recover a valid signature; handle then invokes the processor.

findings.title: Restore constant-time signature comparison
findings.whyItBreaks: String equality is not guaranteed to take constant time. Replacing hmac.compare_digest makes signature verification a timing oracle for attacker-supplied signatures on the path that authorizes processor(payload).

findings.whyItBreaks: The transaction commits the ledger entry at line 23 before either balance update runs. If an update fails, the ledger entry remains committed; if the second update fails, the source balance may also have changed without the destination balance changing.

findings.title: Keep the balance updates inside the transaction
findings.whyItBreaks: The transaction ends after the ledger insert. If either balance update fails, the error propagates but the ledger entry has already committed. If the second update fails, the source account may also have been debited without a matching credit.

findings.title: Keep both balance updates inside the ledger transaction
findings.whyItBreaks: The ledger entry commits before either balance update. If a balance update fails, the ledger records a transfer that did not complete. If the credit fails after the debit succeeds, funds are removed without reaching the destination.

findings.title: Restore UTC calendar fields for billing days
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous implementation used UTC fields. In Asia/Taipei, billingDay(2026-09-23T23:30:00Z) now returns 2026-09-24 instead of 2026-09-23. sameBillingDay also compares these shifted dates, so billing-day classification varies by host timezone.

findings.title: Preserve UTC when deriving the billing day
findings.whyItBreaks: In America/Los_Angeles, billingDay(new Date('2026-01-01T00:30:00Z')) now returns '2025-12-31' instead of '2026-01-01'. sameBillingDay also inherits this change, so billing-day results vary with the host time zone.

findings.title: Restore UTC date components for billing days
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous implementation used UTC components. With TZ=America/Los_Angeles, 2024-01-02T00:30:00Z now returns 2024-01-01. sameBillingDay also incorrectly treats that instant and 2024-01-01T23:30:00Z as the same UTC billing day.

findings.title: Include the tenant in the cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: After readProfile('tenantA', 'shared', ...) caches a profile, readProfile('tenantB', 'shared', ...) uses the same key. The cache hit at line 16 returns tenantA’s profile without fetching tenantB’s.

findings.title: Include the tenant in the profile cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: After readProfile('tenantA', 'alice') caches a profile, readProfile('tenantB', 'alice') uses the same key. The cache hit returns tenantA’s profile without calling fetchProfile for tenantB.

findings.title: Include the tenant in the profile cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: After reading an account in tenant A, reading the same account name in tenant B finds A's cached profile and returns it without calling fetchProfile for B.

findings.title: Preserve errors from missing keys
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported load function previously threw for a missing key. It now returns "", which is also a valid stored value, so callers cannot distinguish failure from success. loadAll likewise returns an array containing "" instead of propagating the error.

findings.title: Preserve the missing-key error
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported load function now returns an empty string when a key is missing, which is indistinguishable from a stored empty string. loadAll also returns an array containing that fallback instead of propagating the missing-key error.

findings.title: Preserve the error when a key cannot be loaded
findings.whyItBreaks: A missing key previously threw an error. It now returns "", which is indistinguishable from a stored empty string. loadAll consequently returns a successful-looking result containing "" for missing keys.

findings.title: Preserve the existing timeoutMs configuration
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing TypeScript callers using Config no longer compile: timeoutMs was removed and retries became required. Existing JavaScript callers pass timeoutMs, so config.timeout is undefined, the deadline becomes NaN, and the timeout guard never rejects another attempt.

findings.title: Run the initial attempt when retries is zero
findings.whyItBreaks: With retries: 0, the loop rejects i=0 and never calls fn. A retry count of zero should still allow the initial attempt; the current body treats retries as total attempts.

findings.title: Expose failure from retryBackground
findings.whyItBreaks: Every failed attempt is caught, and exhausting retries returns the same void value as success. This new public API gives callers no way to distinguish a failed operation from a completed one.

findings.title: Preserve the timeoutMs config field for existing callers
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing callers supplying the former Config shape no longer type-check. At runtime, retry reads an absent timeout field, making its deadline NaN and disabling its timeout check.

findings.title: Run the initial attempt when retries is zero
findings.whyItBreaks: For config.retries = 0, the loop never enters and fn is never called. A retry count of zero should disable additional attempts, not the initial attempt.

findings.title: Expose failure after background retries are exhausted
findings.whyItBreaks: The new public function returns void both when fn succeeds and when every attempt throws. A caller cannot distinguish a failed operation from a completed one.

findings.title: Preserve the existing timeoutMs config field
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing callers pass { maxAttempts, timeoutMs }. They now fail TypeScript checking because timeout is required; JavaScript callers produce a NaN deadline, so retry never enforces their timeout. Requiring retries also breaks callers of retry that do not use retryBackground.

findings.title: Include the initial attempt when counting retries
findings.whyItBreaks: The public retries field promises retries in addition to an initial attempt, but the loop uses it as the total attempt count. With retries: 0, the callback is never called; with retries: 1, it is called only once.

findings.title: Expose failure after background retries are exhausted
findings.whyItBreaks: The new public function catches every callback error and returns void after the last attempt. Its caller cannot distinguish repeated failure from a successful callback.

findings.title: Display the supplied value in the input
findings.whyItBreaks: A string value such as "abc" previously appeared in the input as "abc"; it now appears as "len=3".

findings.title: Display the supplied value in the input
findings.whyItBreaks: A string value such as "abc" now renders as "len=3" instead of "abc", changing the field's visible and submitted value.

findings.title: Handle number values according to the new prop type
findings.whyItBreaks: FieldProps now accepts numbers, but a number has no length property. Passing 42 renders "len=undefined".

findings.title: Handle numeric values before reading length
findings.whyItBreaks: The public value type now permits numbers, but number.length is undefined. A numeric value renders `len=undefined`, and TypeScript rejects the property access.

findings.title: Remove the token from workflow output
findings.whyItBreaks: The shell expands TOKEN into stdout on every push. GitHub's log masking is a safeguard, but emitting the credential makes its confidentiality depend on that safeguard.

findings.title: Remove the token from workflow output
findings.whyItBreaks: The step expands secrets.TOKEN into stdout. GitHub's log masking is a safeguard, but emitting the credential creates an unnecessary disclosure path; the build step does not use the token.

findings.title: Remove the token from deploy output
findings.whyItBreaks: The command writes the raw TOKEN value to stdout. GitHub log masking may hide it in the displayed log, but the workflow should not emit a credential and depend on masking to protect it.

findings.title: Restore the Git subprocess output limit
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing maxBuffer restores spawnSync's 1 MiB default. The git diff call at line 140 can exceed that limit on a large PR, causing the subprocess to fail and runGithub to abort without reviewing the PR.

findings.title: Restore the Git output buffer limit
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing maxBuffer lowers spawnSync's output limit from 64 MiB to its 1 MiB default. A PR diff over that limit makes the git diff call fail before review runs.

findings.title: Restore the Git output buffer for PR diffs
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing the 64 MiB maxBuffer restores Node's 1 MiB default. A PR patch larger than that makes spawnSync fail; the status check at line 38 then throws before review(bundle) runs.

findings.title: Keep the bundle base SHA aligned with its patch
findings.whyItBreaks: The patch and changed-file list are computed from mergeBase at lines 140–141, but the bundle now reports baseSha, which can be a later base-branch commit. When the base branch has advanced, the reported SHA pair describes a different diff from the patch supplied for review.

findings.title: Restore the read-only sandbox for Codex reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing `-s read-only` makes the spawned Codex process use its configured sandbox. If that configuration permits writes, code being reviewed can cause the review process to modify repository files.

findings.title: Restore the read-only sandbox for PR review
findings.whyItBreaks: runCodex executes in the repository at line 24. Removing `-s read-only` makes filesystem access depend on the caller's Codex configuration, so a review can modify the checkout when that configuration permits writes.

findings.title: Restore the read-only sandbox for review runs
findings.whyItBreaks: The removed -s read-only argument was the function's explicit write restriction. Codex can otherwise inherit a workspace-write or full-access setting, allowing a review prompt to modify the repository passed as cwd.

findings.title: Diff from the merge base of the PR commits
findings.whyItBreaks: When PR_BASE_SHA is the base branch tip and that branch advanced after the PR diverged, diffing directly from baseSha includes those base-branch changes in reverse. Both the patch sent for review and changedFiles can then describe changes the PR did not make.

findings.title: Diff against the PR head commit
findings.whyItBreaks: PR_HEAD_SHA can identify the PR commit while the checkout's HEAD identifies a different commit, such as a pull-request merge commit. The patch and changedFiles then come from HEAD, but the review is posted with commit_id=headSha. The reviewer may assess different content, and inline comment positions may not match the posted commit.

findings.title: Diff from the merge base when the base branch has advanced
findings.whyItBreaks: When PR_BASE_SHA is a base-branch tip newer than the PR's fork point, diffing that tip against the PR branch also includes base-only changes as reverse changes. The patch and changedFiles can then describe files the PR did not change, leading to incorrect review findings and inline comments.

findings.title: Generate the review patch from the PR head SHA
findings.whyItBreaks: PR_HEAD_SHA can identify the PR commit while the checkout's HEAD is a merge commit. The patch now ends at that merge commit, but the review and check are posted against PR_HEAD_SHA. The reviewer can therefore assess different code from the commit receiving its verdict.

findings.title: Diff from the merge base when reviewing the PR head
findings.whyItBreaks: When HEAD is the PR head and PR_BASE_SHA is the current target-branch tip, commits added to the target branch since the PR diverged appear as reverse changes in the patch and changed-file list. The review can attribute unrelated changes to the PR.

findings.title: Use the PR head SHA for the review patch
findings.whyItBreaks: On a checkout where HEAD is GitHub's synthetic merge commit, the patch describes that merge result while the review is submitted with commit_id=headSha. Merge conflict resolutions or base-branch changes can make the patch and its line numbers differ from the PR head, producing incorrect findings or rejected inline comments.

findings.title: Preserve literal dollar sequences in prompt substitutions
findings.whyItBreaks: String.replace interprets sequences such as $& and $' in a replacement string. If a patch contains literal $&, the generated prompts contain the placeholder text instead of that patch content. The critic can then assess a corrupted diff. The previous callback replacements preserved these sequences literally.

findings.title: Preserve literal text when substituting prompt placeholders
findings.whyItBreaks: String.replace interprets dollar-sign sequences in a replacement string. A patch containing `$$` reaches the reviewer as `$`, while `$&` becomes the placeholder text. The bundle, candidate findings, and critic patch can therefore be altered before review.

findings.title: Restore literal insertion for prompt data
findings.whyItBreaks: String.replace interprets tokens such as $& and $' in a replacement string. If a bundle, candidate finding, or patch contains one, the prompt receives substituted text instead of the original data. For example, $& in bundle.patch becomes {{PATCH}}, so the critic reviews a corrupted patch.

findings.title: Keep the reviewed commit in the fallback review
findings.whyItBreaks: If the PR receives a new commit while Needlefish reviews the captured head SHA and the first review request fails, this fallback omits commit_id. GitHub then associates the review with the PR's most recent commit, although the verdict and body describe the older commit. The check run still targets the captured SHA. [GitHub documents this default](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews).

findings.title: Keep the reviewed commit ID in the fallback request
findings.whyItBreaks: If the first review request fails and the PR receives a new commit before the fallback runs, omitting commit_id makes GitHub attach the fallback review to that new commit. A REQUEST_CHANGES review can then govern code Needlefish did not review, while its check remains attached to the original head SHA.

findings.title: Keep the reviewed commit in the fallback request
findings.whyItBreaks: If the first review request fails and the PR receives a new commit before the fallback runs, omitting commit_id makes GitHub attach the fallback review to that new commit. Needlefish reviewed the earlier headSha, and postCheck still reports against that earlier SHA. GitHub documents that an omitted commit_id defaults to the PR's most recent commit: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews

findings.title: Reject invalid severity instead of assigning P1
findings.whyItBreaks: An absent or unrecognized severity previously raised an error. It now becomes P1, so callers cannot distinguish malformed review output from a real P1 finding.

findings.title: Restore validation of required finding fields and locations
findings.whyItBreaks: A finding with no file, title, explanation, fix, or valid line number now passes normalization. Missing locations become an empty file and line 0, and invalid numeric locations can become NaN. The public function returns these as a Finding, concealing malformed input from callers.

findings.title: Reject malformed findings instead of returning fabricated values
findings.whyItBreaks: An input with an invalid severity and no file or line now returns a Finding with severity P1, an empty file, and lineStart 0. Previously these errors reached the caller as exceptions. The exported API therefore presents invalid review data as a valid finding and makes the original failure indistinguishable from a real P1 finding.

findings.title: Preserve the non-strict normalizeReview path
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported function previously accepted a second argument, strict=false, and skipped malformed findings. Removing that parameter breaks typed callers using the existing signature; the new unconditional map also stops skipping malformed entries.

findings.title: Reject invalid findings instead of manufacturing valid-looking values
findings.whyItBreaks: normalizeFinding({}) now returns a Finding with severity P1, an empty file, and zero line numbers. These fields previously caused validation errors. The exported function therefore presents malformed review output as a real finding with an invented severity and unusable location.

findings.title: Preserve the non-strict normalizeReview API
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported function previously accepted a second strict=false argument that skipped malformed findings. Removing that parameter breaks TypeScript callers on upgrade, and the unconditional map no longer provides that behavior.

findings.title: Restore explicit repository selection for manual reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: On workflow_dispatch, these commands run before actions/checkout. In a clean runner workspace, gh has no repository context, so both lookups fail. The surrounding echo commands still write empty head and base outputs, and checkout then lacks the intended PR head ref.

findings.title: Restore explicit repository selection for manual reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: On workflow_dispatch, these gh commands run before checkout. Without -R or GH_REPO, gh has no repository to resolve on a clean runner. The commands produce no SHAs, so the review cannot target the requested PR.

findings.title: Restore explicit repository selection when resolving PR refs
findings.whyItBreaks: On workflow_dispatch, these commands run before checkout. Without -R, gh must infer a repository from the self-hosted runner's working directory. An empty workspace has no repository; a reused workspace may point to another one. The commands then fail or return the wrong PR's refs, and the echo commands can write empty outputs despite gh failing.

findings.title: Reject malformed review output before normalizing it
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported function now converts missing or invalid required fields into empty strings and arrays. For example, normalizeReview(undefined) returns a RawReview instead of signaling malformed output, so callers cannot distinguish failure from a legitimate empty review.

findings.title: Reject malformed review output instead of defaulting it
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported function previously threw when required review fields were missing or malformed. It now turns missing findings and residual risks into empty arrays, so callers cannot distinguish failed or incomplete output from a review with no findings or risks.

findings.title: Preserve errors for malformed review output
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported normalizeReview function now turns null or an object missing required fields into a RawReview with an empty summary and empty arrays. Callers cannot distinguish malformed output from a legitimate review with no findings; previously these inputs threw validation errors.

findings.title: Restore PR ref resolution for manual reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: On workflow_dispatch, pull_request.head.sha is absent, so checkout uses github.ref, the branch selected to run the workflow, regardless of pr_number. The review then runs against that branch instead of the requested PR. The same event also leaves PR_BASE_SHA and PR_HEAD_SHA empty at lines 45–46; the removed step previously resolved all three PR refs.

findings.title: Resolve the requested PR head before checkout
findings.whyItBreaks: A workflow_dispatch event has no pull_request.head.sha, so this expression selects github.ref. When the selected workflow branch differs from the PR named by pr_number, the Install and review steps run that branch's code instead of the requested PR's code.

findings.title: Resolve the requested PR head before manual checkout
findings.whyItBreaks: On workflow_dispatch, the pull_request head SHA is absent, so this expression selects github.ref. If the workflow is dispatched from a branch other than the requested PR head, Install and Needlefish review run that branch's code while --pr names the requested PR. The removed Resolve PR refs step previously checked out the PR head by its resolved SHA.

findings.title: Restore a sufficient buffer for git diff
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing maxBuffer lowers the git subprocess limit from 64 MiB to Node's 1 MiB default. A git diff above that limit ends with ENOBUFS, so runLocal throws before it can review the patch.

findings.title: Restore the Git output buffer for large diffs
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing maxBuffer lowers spawnSync's output limit from 64 MiB to its 1 MiB default. runLocal reads the full patch through this helper, so a diff over that limit causes Git collection to fail and the review never runs.

findings.title: Restore a buffer large enough for review diffs
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing maxBuffer reduces spawnSync's output limit from 64 MiB to its 1 MiB default. runLocal passes the complete git diff through this helper, so a diff over 1 MiB causes spawnSync to fail before review(bundle) runs.

findings.title: Mark review errors as failed checks
findings.whyItBreaks: When review() or posting the review throws, this path completes the Needlefish check with `neutral`. GitHub treats `neutral` as successful for required status checks, so a PR can satisfy the Needlefish requirement without a completed review. The process exit code does not change that custom check's conclusion. See [GitHub's required-check rules](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/troubleshooting-required-status-checks).

findings.title: Post the check on the commit GitHub is evaluating
findings.whyItBreaks: On a standard pull_request checkout, local `HEAD` is the test merge commit while `pr.head.sha` is the branch commit. The new value flows to `postCheck` as `head_sha`. When the test merge commit has a status, GitHub evaluates required checks on that merge commit, so the Needlefish check posted to the branch commit does not satisfy the requirement and an otherwise approvable PR remains blocked. See [GitHub's commit selection rules](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/troubleshooting-required-status-checks).

findings.title: Mark review errors as failed checks
findings.whyItBreaks: The catch path now posts a neutral conclusion. GitHub treats neutral checks as satisfying required checks, so a review error can permit a PR to merge without a completed review. The process exit code does not change the posted check conclusion.

findings.title: Select the repository explicitly for PR diff retrieval
findings.whyItBreaks: runGithub accepts a checkout path, but ghText runs in the process's current directory. When that differs from cwd, `gh pr diff` may select another repository or fail to identify one. This occurs before the review error handler, leaving no check result.

findings.title: Mark review errors as failed checks
findings.whyItBreaks: When review or posting throws, this path creates a completed Needlefish check with conclusion `neutral`. GitHub accepts `neutral` as successful for a required status check, so that check can permit a merge even though the review failed. The stderr message and process exit code do not change the conclusion of this check. [GitHub's required-check documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/troubleshooting-required-status-checks) lists `neutral` among successful conclusions.

findings.title: Restore a checkout that contains the review tool
findings.whyItBreaks: The head SHA contains only .github/workflows/review.yml and .needlefish/answers.json. With the separate tool checkout removed, this step runs pnpm install in a directory with no package.json or lockfile, and the later src/cli.ts path is absent. The review job cannot run.

findings.title: Keep PR-controlled code out of the reviewer process
findings.whyItBreaks: The job now executes src/cli.ts from the PR head with GH_TOKEN and pull-request/checks write permissions. A same-repository PR that supplies this file can alter or suppress its own review and use the token during that step.

facts.meaning: The workflow executes Needlefish's reviewer implementation from the untrusted PR-head checkout.
The PR-controlled reviewer can write pull-request reviews or checks.
The workflow executes Needlefish's reviewer implementation from the untrusted PR-head checkout.

findings.title: Restore a trusted checkout for the review tool
findings.whyItBreaks: The command executes src/cli.ts from the PR head with GH_TOKEN available. A same-repository PR can change that file; a manually dispatched review can also select a fork PR because the job condition permits workflow_dispatch. The PR code then runs on a self-hosted runner with pull-request and checks write permissions.

findings.title: Install the tool from a checkout that contains its package files
findings.whyItBreaks: Both base and head trees contain only the workflow and .needlefish/answers.json. The PR checkout has no package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, or src/cli.ts, so the install and subsequent CLI command cannot complete.

facts.meaning: The workflow executes Needlefish's reviewer implementation from the untrusted PR-head checkout.
The PR-controlled reviewer can write pull-request reviews or checks.
The workflow executes Needlefish's reviewer implementation from the untrusted PR-head checkout.
The PR-controlled reviewer can write pull-request reviews or checks.

findings.title: Restore a checkout containing the reviewer
findings.whyItBreaks: The head commit contains neither package.json nor src/cli.ts. After removing the separate tool checkout, the install step has no package manifest and the review command has no CLI to run, so the job cannot review this PR.

findings.title: Keep PR-controlled code out of the privileged review job
findings.whyItBreaks: On same-repository PRs, these steps install dependencies and execute the PR head's code on a self-hosted runner. The job grants pull-request and checks write permissions, and the review step supplies GITHUB_TOKEN. A PR can therefore make its package scripts or CLI execute arbitrary code with the review job's access.

facts.meaning: The workflow executes Needlefish's reviewer implementation from the untrusted PR-head checkout.
The PR-controlled reviewer can write pull-request reviews or checks.
The workflow executes Needlefish's reviewer implementation from the untrusted PR-head checkout.

findings.title: Preserve severity normalization before applying the fallback
findings.whyItBreaks: normalizeReview passes unchecked findings to normalizeFinding. A severity of " p0 " previously normalized to P0; the new exact-match check rejects it and reports P3, concealing a critical finding.

findings.title: Restore severity normalization before validation
findings.whyItBreaks: A finding with severity "p0" or " P0 " previously normalized to P0. The exact-match check now returns P3, misclassifying a critical finding as low severity.

findings.title: Keep malformed severities from defaulting to P3
findings.whyItBreaks: An unrecognized or missing severity previously became P1. It now becomes P3 without an error signal, so callers of this exported normalization path receive a low-severity finding they cannot distinguish from a genuine P3.

findings.title: Preserve severity normalization before validation
findings.whyItBreaks: For raw.severity = " p0 ", the previous implementation returned P0. The new includes check rejects that value and returns P3. normalizeReview uses this function for every finding, so a critical finding can be reported as low severity.

findings.title: Keep GitHub tokens out of the Codex subprocess
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing the explicit environment makes spawnSync inherit process.env. A Codex run reviewing untrusted PR text can therefore access GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, and GITHUB_API_TOKEN through its subprocess tools, exposing credentials across the review boundary.

findings.title: Keep GitHub tokens out of the Codex subprocess
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing the filtered env option makes spawnSync inherit process.env. Any GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, or GITHUB_API_TOKEN in the parent is now available to the Codex subprocess, including commands it runs while inspecting the repository.

findings.title: Restore GitHub token filtering for the Codex subprocess
findings.whyItBreaks: Without an explicit env option, spawnSync inherits process.env. A Codex process reviewing repository content can now access GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, and GITHUB_API_TOKEN from its parent; the previous code removed all three before spawning it.

findings.title: Restore the fork guard before running PR code
findings.whyItBreaks: A fork PR now reaches this self-hosted job. The workflow checks out the fork's head commit, then runs pnpm install and src/cli.ts from that checkout. A fork author can therefore execute code on the runner. GitHub warns that untrusted PR code can persistently compromise a self-hosted runner: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use

findings.title: Restore the fork guard before running PR code
findings.whyItBreaks: The removed condition allowed this job only for branches in the repository. A fork PR can now reach the self-hosted runner, which checks out the fork's head SHA and runs dependency installation and its CLI. The fork author can supply code executed on that runner.

findings.title: Restore the fork guard before running PR code
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing this job-level condition allows fork PRs to reach checkout, run pnpm install from the PR head, and execute its src/cli.ts on a self-hosted runner. A fork author controls that code and can execute arbitrary commands on the runner.

findings.title: Preserve zero-valued timeout overrides
findings.whyItBreaks: Both runner timeout environment variables previously accepted 0. Now a 0 grace period becomes 5000 ms, delaying SIGKILL after SIGTERM; a 0 give-up period becomes 2000 ms, delaying the result after SIGKILL.

findings.title: Preserve zero as a valid runner grace period
findings.whyItBreaks: With NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS=0, the previous code scheduled SIGKILL immediately after SIGTERM. The new check substitutes the 5000 ms fallback, so a process that ignores SIGTERM remains running for five more seconds. The same change substitutes 2000 ms for an explicitly configured zero give-up delay.

findings.title: Preserve zero-valued runner timeout settings
findings.whyItBreaks: Setting NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS=0 previously scheduled SIGKILL immediately after the runner timed out; it now uses the 5000 ms fallback. Setting NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_SIGKILL_GIVE_UP_MS=0 likewise changes immediate completion after SIGKILL to a 2000 ms wait.

findings.title: Restore coverage for changed files outside selected hotspots
findings.whyItBreaks: The selected hotspots are now the entire deep-review workload. If mapping omits a changed file, or its hotspot falls outside the six selected, that file receives no deep review and the result does not flag the omission.

findings.title: Preserve deep-review residual risks
findings.whyItBreaks: A deep review can report a blocking residual risk, but the merged candidate always gives the critic an empty residual_risks array. The resulting verdict can therefore omit that blocker.

findings.title: Deep-review every changed file
findings.whyItBreaks: The removed coverage backstop means a changed file omitted by the map pass, or present only in a hotspot beyond the six-hotspot limit, receives no deep review. The review can still return a verdict without examining that file.

findings.title: Preserve blocking risks from deep reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: A deep pass can report an unresolved risk with blocks=true, but candidateMerged now gives the critic an empty residual_risks array. The critic and final verdict can therefore treat an unresolved review as clear.

findings.title: Keep distinct findings on the same line
findings.whyItBreaks: Two findings with the same file, start line, category, and title but different failure explanations now share a key. dedup keeps only one, so a separate defect can disappear before the critic sees it.

findings.title: Restore coverage for changed files outside selected hotspots
findings.whyItBreaks: The removed coverage backstop means a changed file omitted by the map pass, or present only in a hotspot beyond the six selected, receives no deep review. The review can then return a verdict without examining that file.

findings.title: Carry deep review residual risks into the critic pass
findings.whyItBreaks: Deep review results can contain blocking residual risks, but this path now passes an empty list to the critic. Those risks cannot reach the final verdict through the merged review.

findings.title: Pass the requested focus to large PR review prompts
findings.whyItBreaks: When a bundle specifies focus, reviewLarge now omits it from both the map bundle and the deep prompt. Neither review pass receives the requested review scope.

findings.title: Pass the requested focus to large-PR review prompts
findings.whyItBreaks: The large-PR path previously passed bundle.focus to both the map and each deep-review prompt. After these deletions, no large-PR prompt receives it, so a focused review request is ignored.

findings.title: Preserve the requested focus in large reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: The large-review path no longer includes bundle.focus in the map bundle or substitutes it into the deep prompt. A focused large-PR review therefore loses the caller's requested focus, while the small-review path still passes the full bundle.

findings.title: Round before splitting minutes and seconds
findings.whyItBreaks: For 119,500 ms, the new calculation produces 1m 60s instead of 2m 0s. renderMarkdown displays this for both call durations and the total duration.

findings.title: Carry rounded seconds into minutes
findings.whyItBreaks: For 119,500 ms, minutes is 1 and the rounded remainder is 60 seconds, so the review renders `1m 60s` instead of `2m 0s`. This affects both call durations and total duration.

findings.title: Carry rounded seconds into minutes
findings.whyItBreaks: At 119,500 ms, minutes is 1 while the rounded remainder is 60 seconds, so the review displays 1m 60s. At 59,500 ms, it displays 60s instead of 1m 0s. Both per-call and total durations use this formatter.

findings.title: Reject zero in the positive-integer parser
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported parsePositiveInteger function promises a positive result, but the changed check returns 0 for "0", an empty string, or whitespace. Callers can no longer rely on its result being greater than zero.

findings.title: Reject zero in parsePositiveInteger
findings.whyItBreaks: Number('0') is 0 and Number.isInteger(0) is true, so the changed condition returns 0 despite the exported function's positive-integer contract. Empty input also becomes 0 through Number('').

findings.title: Reject zero in parsePositiveInteger
findings.whyItBreaks: Number('0') is 0, which passes the new check and is returned. The exported function promises a positive integer and its error says the same; zero is not positive.
